GreedyKS sketch of the one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic

Source: R/dfr_greedyks.R
greedyks.Rd

Online approximation of the statistic D = sup |F_n(x) - F(x)| of the one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test between a stream and a reference distribution with CDF F, in O(log m) time per observation and O(m) memory, whatever the number of observations (Cardoso and Galeno, 2023).

Usage

greedyks(cdf, m = 100, min_instances = 0)

greedyks_update(sketch, x)

greedyks_statistic(sketch)

greedyks_pvalue(sketch, exact = TRUE)

Arguments

cdf

Cumulative distribution function of the reference distribution (for example function(x) pnorm(x, 1, 1)).

m

Number of buckets (the memory units of the paper).

min_instances

Number of observations before the statistic is estimated (it is 0 before).

sketch

A greedyks sketch.

x

Numeric vector of observations, processed in order. Missing values are skipped.

exact

Passed to ks_sf(): the exact distribution of the statistic (TRUE, the default, as scipy.stats.kstwo in the reference) or the limiting Kolmogorov distribution (FALSE).

Value

greedyks() returns a greedyks sketch. greedyks_update() returns the sketch after the observations x, in order. greedyks_statistic() returns the estimate of D, and greedyks_pvalue() its p-value for the number of observations processed (see ks_sf()).

Details

Each observation x is mapped to f = F(x) and to the bucket b = ceiling(f m) of 0, ..., m, which keeps the number of observations and the smallest and largest f it received. The largest gaps between the ECDF and the CDF, D+ and D-, are updated greedily (Algorithm 2 of the paper): with the bucket just updated and with the buckets that gave the current maxima, re-evaluated at every step. The counts before a bucket come from a Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree). The estimate is max(D+, D-).

The reference implementation uses ceiling(f m) (the paper writes floor), so there are m + 1 buckets; heimdall does the same.

References

Cardoso, D. O. and Galeno, T. D. (2023). Online evaluation of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on arbitrarily large samples. Journal of Computational Science, 67, 101959. doi:10.1016/j.jocs.2023.101959

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- rnorm(5000, 1.1, 1)
sketch <- greedyks_update(greedyks(function(q) pnorm(q, 1, 1), m = 100), x)
greedyks_statistic(sketch)
#> [1] 0.04062458
unname(ks.test(x, "pnorm", 1, 1)$statistic)   # exact value
#> [1] 0.04101958
greedyks_pvalue(sketch)
#> [1] 1.316868e-07
